Char: Participants: Participants were: (1) Aged ≥50 years, (2) ethnic Chinese, (3) diagnosed with clinical depression by a clinical psychiatrist, (4) presented with at least mild depression assessed by Beck depression inventory (BDI), and (5) using antidepressant medications. Participants with severe depression were included to enhance the generalizability of this study.Mean age (1) Control: 60.5 years (SD 7.3); Moderate walking group 60.6 years (SD 3.1); Vigorous walking group 59.6 years (SD 4.6); Women 73.33%.
Char: Interventions:
Aerobic exercise: the exercise intensity and session duration in MOD [moderate walking] and VIG [vigorous walking] were set to 3.5 Metabolic Equivalents of Task (METs) for 50 minutes and 7 METs for 25 minutes, respectively. Walking exercise sessions were conducted on treadmills under the supervision of research personnel three times per week for 12 weeks. Heart rate was monitored during the walking exercise sessions to ensure the prescribed exercise intensity was reached.  Participants in MOD and VIG were supervised to maintain their heart rates within the THR ranges during the walking exercise sessions (THR ± 10 beats per minute).

Comparator: No intervention given. Participants continued antidepressant treatment during 12-week period, instructed to maintain their lifestyle routines, including daily diet and habitual physical activity.
